title: SDK multimodal sample app blueprint and UX guidelines
author: Aisha Rao
body:
Overview

Purpose:
This page provides a compact, production-minded blueprint for a multimodal sample application built with Redwood SDKs (client + server patterns). The goal is to give developers a ready-to-run reference that demonstrates: image + text prompts, streaming responses, result enrichment with embeddings, cost-aware batching, and UX patterns for predictable latency and graceful degradation.

Audience:
- SDK users building multimodal front-ends
- Developer advocates creating example apps
- Support engineers diagnosing common integration issues

Quick summary (2 lines):
Provide a small end-to-end example demonstrating: 1) a browser or mobile client sending text+image prompts to Redwood API via the SDK; 2) server-side orchestration that routes to appropriate model variants, caches image embeddings, and streams token-level updates to the client.

Design principles
- Predictable latency: surface an upper-bound latency to the user and enable progressive partial results (streaming).
- Cost transparency: log per-request token & image embedding cost to telemetry for optimization experiments.
- Resilience-first: local fallback (reduced-quality model) on timeouts, with clear UX affordances.
- Minimal friction: single-file example for quickstarts, with optional feature toggles for advanced behavior.

Architecture overview
- Client (browser/mobile): captures text and image(s), displays a progressive response UI, and shows quality/cost indicators.
- Backend proxy (Node/Go/Python): validates requests, applies tenant quotas, invokes Redwood SDK, manages caching and batching, and emits telemetry.
- Redwood inference: model catalog selection (image-capable model, text-only fallback), streaming responses, embeddings endpoint.
- Cache store: Redis for prefix/KV and image embedding cache.

Key flows
1) Image+text prompt flow:
   - Client: captures image (base64 or multipart) and text; sends to backend with small metadata (image_size, intent).
   - Backend: check image_embedding_cache; if miss, call /embeddings endpoint (batched) and store embedding with TTL 7d.
   - Backend: call /generate with model variant selection (see routing policy table). Use streaming for first N tokens then aggregate.
   - Client: render streaming tokens and a placeholder for final structured output.

2) Embeddings-only flow (search/enrichment):
   - Client or batch job maps images and candidate text to embeddings, then sends a nearest-neighbors query to rank candidates server-side before final generation.

Routing policy (example table)
- Purpose: decide model variant by desired latency, cost tier, and input size.

Model purpose | Latency target | Model variant | Fallback
Short chat | <200ms first-byte | small-quantized-2x | small-quantized-cpu
Image caption | <500ms per-step | image-capable-8k | text-only+ocr-fallback
Long-form generation | burst-tolerant | large-32k-fp16 | large-16k-quant

SDK patterns and code samples
- Note: snippets below use the official Redwood JavaScript SDK pattern. Replace with Python/Go equivalents in the repo samples.

1) Client: streaming handler (browser)
```js
const ws = new WebSocket('/sse-proxy');
ws.onmessage = (ev) => {
  const payload = JSON.parse(ev.data);
  if (payload.type === 'token') appendTokenToUI(payload.text);
  if (payload.type === 'done') showFinalCard(payload.result);
};
// send image as multipart to backend
```

2) Server: batched embedding call and generate orchestration (Node/Express pseudocode)\```js
// batcher: groups embedding requests for 50ms then sends a single /embeddings call
batcher.add(request, (embedding) => {
  // attach embedding to request and continue orchestration
});

// orchestration: pick model and call Redwood SDK
const model = pickModelByPolicy({inputTokens, clientTier});
const stream = redwood.generate({model, prompt: promptWithEmbedding, stream: true});
stream.on('data', (chunk) => proxyToClient(chunk));
stream.on('end', () => finalizeResponse());
```

3) Client fallback flow (pseudocode)\```js
const response = await fetch('/api/generate', {timeout: 2500});
if (!response.ok || response.timedOut) {
  // show degraded UI and optionally re-issue with lower-cost model
  showErrorOverlay('Response delayed. Showing cached result or quick summary.');
}
```

Telemetry and observability
- Events to emit per request:
  - request_id, tenant_id, model_variant, input_tokens, output_tokens, image_size_bytes, embedding_cache_hit (bool), duration_ms, cost_estimate_cents
- SLOs to track:
  - P95 end-to-end latency by route (chat, caption, embed) < configured target
  - Embedding cache hit rate > 70% for repeated assets
  - Streaming first-byte latency P50 < 150ms for chat flows
- Dashboards suggested:
  - 'Multimodal API': throughput, errors, avg token cost, cache hit heatmap by tenant
  - 'Sample app health': per-example telemetry, user-visible degraded-flow count

Feature toggles and runtime config (table)
- toggle_name | description | default
- enable_embedding_cache | Use Redis to cache image embeddings | true
- streaming_enabled | Send token-level updates to clients | true
- model_routing_mode | auto|manual|canary | auto
- low_latency_fallback_ms | threshold to trigger fallback | 1200

UX patterns and copy guidance
- Progressive rendering: show partial text as tokens arrive; avoid flicker by reserving space for long-form answers.
- Latency affordance: display a subtle ETA bar at request start (calculated from historical medians).
- Cost transparency: optional developer toggle in the sample app to annotate responses with approximate token cost. Useful for demos.
- Fallback messaging: Be explicit — "Using a low-latency fallback; quality may be lower." Avoid technical jargon for end-users.

Common integration pitfalls and canonical fixes
1) Large image uploads cause timeouts:
   - Fix: upload to a presigned object store and send reference; calculate embedding server-side. Ensure backend accepts small metadata only.
2) Missing or inconsistent streaming boundaries:
   - Fix: standardize chunk envelope (type, seq, timestamp) and use a reconnect+resume token.
3) Embedding TTLs too short, causing repeated cost spikes:
   - Fix: extend TTL for stable assets to 7–30 days depending on size and privacy. Add eviction TTL for ephemeral uploads.
4) Telemetry mismatch between client/server:
   - Fix: generate a single request_id at the edge and propagate through headers. Instrument at three points (edge, backend, redwood).

Operational runbook (quick checklist)
- Symptoms: cascading slow responses for image prompts, high embedding costs, or spike in streaming disconnects.
- Immediate steps:
  1) Check embedding queue depth and Redis latency.
  2) Inspect per-tenant model routing decisions and fallback counts in the last 10m.
  3) Verify CDN/presigned upload success rate and median upload times.
  4) If streaming disconnect rate > 2%, enable the non-streaming fallback for new requests and investigate network errors.

Rollout guide for example app
1) Ship as an opt-in sample (feature-flagged) for internal users.
2) Run a 2-week pilot with the telemetry toggles enabled to collect: embedding cache hit, avg per-request cost, fallback frequency.
3) Iterate UX copy and token cost estimator based on pilot data.
4) Open-source the sample with a trimmed config file and 'safe defaults' (no retention beyond 7d, obfuscate tenant ids).

Files included in repo (suggested)
- README.md (quickstart + security notes)
- server/ (backend orchestrator and batcher)
- client/ (production example and a minimal dev-only preset)
- infra/ (redis, presigned-upload sample, feature flag config)
- telemetry/ (dashboard JSONs and example export pipeline)

Security and privacy notes
- Images may contain PII; default to opt-in storage and do not persist raw images unless customer explicitly enables storage.
- Encrypt embedding payloads at rest if retention > 24h.
- Provide a debug-mode that strips tenant ids for public example runs.

Appendix A — small checklist for SDK authors adding multimodal helpers
- Provide a single-call integration that accepts file references (presigned URL) and handles embedding cache + generation orchestration internally.
- Expose streaming and non-streaming variants with identical response shapes.
- Include idiomatic samples: React hook, Flutter handler, and a small CLI for batch conversion.

Appendix B — sample API schema (simplified)
- Request:
  {
    "type": "multimodal.generate",
    "image_refs": ["s3://..."],
    "prompt": "Summarize this image for a shopping app",
    "options": {"max_tokens": 256, "stream": true}
  }
- Streaming chunk:
  {"type":"token","seq":45,"text":"..."}
- Final event:
  {"type":"done","structured": {"caption":"...","tags":["shoe","men"]}}
